general_information.crop_description: Rice is a tropical and subtropical cereal grain and the staple food for more than half of the world's population. It is cultivated in flooded (paddy) conditions, though it also grows in well-managed upland systems. It is highly responsive to water, temperature, and nutrient management.
general_information.crop_duration: 110-145 days depending on variety (short, medium, and long duration)
general_information.economic_importance: Rice is the primary food grain of India and a major export commodity. It supports the livelihood of millions of smallholder farmers and is central to national food security and market economies.
major_uses: Staple food grain (consumed as whole grain)
Milling to produce rice, bran, and husk
Straw used as animal fodder and bedding
Broken rice used for brewing and food processing

agro_climatic_zones: Hot humid plains of eastern India
region_suitability.altitude_range: Sea level to 2000 m (most productive below 1000 m)

soil_intelligence.soil_texture: Heavy clay to clay loam with high water-holding capacity
soil_intelligence.organic_matter_requirement: Moderate to high organic matter (1.5-2.5% preferred)
soil_intelligence.drainage_suitability: Poorly drained soils good for paddy; requires controlled drainage for aerobic stages
soil_intelligence.land_preparation_guidelines: Puddle the field to a depth of 10-15 cm for transplanted rice, ensure leveling for uniform water distribution, and incorporate 5-10 tons/ha of well-decomposed FYM or compost before final puddling.

climate_intelligence.harvest_weather: Dry, sunny weather with low humidity; avoid rain during harvest
climate_intelligence.rainfall_requirement: 1000-1500 mm per season (or 1200-1500 mm for rainfed lowland)
climate_intelligence.sunshine_requirement: 6-8 hours bright sunshine daily during vegetative and grain filling
climate_intelligence.wind_sensitivity: Moderate; strong winds at flowering cause sterility and lodging
climate_intelligence.heat_tolerance: Moderate; flowering is most sensitive to heat stress above 35°C
climate_intelligence.cold_frost_tolerance: Low; rice is frost sensitive and cold intolerant (especially at flowering)
climate_intelligence.drought_tolerance: Low to moderate; drought at critical stages severely reduces yield
climate_intelligence.flood_tolerance: Moderate; tolerant of shallow submergence but growth stops with deep flooding

water_intelligence.total_water_requirement: 1200-1800 mm per crop cycle (including effective rainfall)
irrigation_methods: System of Rice Intensification (SRI) — intermittent irrigation
water_intelligence.irrigation_schedule: Maintain 2-5 cm standing water during tillering, increase to 5-7 cm at panicle initiation, keep moist during flowering, and stop irrigation 10-15 days before harvest.
water_intelligence.waterlogging_tolerance: Moderate; rice tolerates shallow water but not prolonged deep submergence
water_intelligence.drainage_requirements: Controlled drainage needed for weeding, mid-season drying, and harvest; avoid waterlogging in vegetative and grain filling stages
water_conservation_practices: Land leveling (laser leveling) for uniform water distribution
Real-time irrigation scheduling based on soil moisture

macronutrient_requirements.Nitrogen (N): 100-120 kg/ha depending on variety and soil

micronutrient_requirements.Zinc: Critical in submerged (puddled) soils; deficiency causes leaf bronzing
micronutrient_requirements.Boron: Aids pollen viability and grain set

stage_wise_fertilizer_schedule.Nursery: Basal nitrogen (20-30 kg/ha) and light phosphorus for seedling vigor
stage_wise_fertilizer_schedule.Tillering: Split nitrogen top dressing (first at 20-25 DAT, second at 40-45 DAT)
stage_wise_fertilizer_schedule.Panicle Initiation: Potassium at 45-50 DAT; nitrogen if needed for panicle development
stage_wise_fertilizer_schedule.Flowering: Limited nitrogen; foliar potassium (2% KNO3) if deficiency
stage_wise_fertilizer_schedule.Grain Filling: Potassium and micronutrients (Zn, B); avoid late nitrogen

organic_alternatives: Green manure (dhaincha, sunn hemp) incorporated before transplanting
Rice straw recycling with nitrogen supplementation
fertilizer_intelligence.deficiency_symptoms: Yellowing of lower leaves (N), purple tinge on older leaves (P), leaf bronzing (Zn), chlorosis of leaf tips (K)
fertilizer_intelligence.toxicity_symptoms: Dark green foliage with excessive vegetative growth (N), iron toxicity (bronzing in acidic soils), salt toxicity (leaf tip burning)
fertilizer_intelligence.soil_test_recommendations: Test soil before planting; apply nutrients based on soil test values and use Leaf Color Chart (LCC) for real-time nitrogen management.

disease_intelligence.symptoms: Blast: diamond-shaped lesions on leaves and neck rot; Bacterial Blight: yellow to white lesions with wavy margins; Sheath Blight: oval lesions on leaf sheath with white fungal growth; Brown Spot: brown circular spots on grains and leaves.
disease_intelligence.causes: Fungal (blast, sheath blight, brown spot), bacterial (bacterial leaf blight), and viral (tungro) pathogens favoured by high humidity, excess nitrogen, dense planting, and water stress.
disease_intelligence.disease_progression: Initially appears as leaf lesions that spread to sheaths, panicles, and grains; severe infection under cool, humid, overcast conditions reduces photosynthesis and grain yield.
disease_intelligence.prevention: Use resistant varieties, balanced nitrogen, proper spacing, field drainage, and clean seed. Avoid dense planting and excess nitrogen.
disease_intelligence.treatment: Apply fungicides (tricyclazole for blast, hexaconazole for sheath blight) at early symptom appearance; remove and destroy infected debris; follow label recommendations.
disease_intelligence.weather_relationships: High humidity and rainfall favour blast and sheath blight; water stress and cold nights favour brown spot; high temperature and humidity favour bacterial blight.

pest_intelligence.symptoms: BPH: hopper burn (yellowing and drying of plants); Stem Borer: dead hearts and whiteheads; Leaf Folder: folded leaves with whitish streaks; Earhead Bug: chaffy grains; Hispa: white streaky feeding lines on leaves.
pest_intelligence.damage: BPH causes rapid plant death in patches; stem borer reduces panicle emergence; leaf folder reduces leaf area; earhead bug damages developing grains reducing yield and quality.
pest_intelligence.prevention: Field hygiene, balanced nitrogen (avoid excess), light traps, resistant varieties, and maintaining natural enemies (spiders, ladybirds).
pest_intelligence.treatment: Apply recommended insecticides (pymetrozine for BPH, chlorantraniliprole for stem borer) at threshold levels; avoid broad-spectrum sprays to protect natural enemies.
pest_intelligence.weather_relationships: Warm, humid conditions and continuous cropping favour BPH outbreaks; dry spells favour stem borer; prolonged leaf wetness increases leaf folder and hispa activity.

market_intelligence.market_seasonality: Kharif (June-November) is the main rice season; rabi/summer rice is limited. Prices peak during lean months (March-May) before the new kharif harvest.
market_intelligence.msp: MSP is declared annually by the Government of India for common grade paddy (refer to the latest MSP notification).
market_intelligence.storage_potential: Good if dried to 12-14% moisture and stored in clean, dry, pest-proof facilities; can store for 6-12 months with proper management.
market_intelligence.transportation_considerations: Grain is bulky and heavy; transport costs are significant. Drying to safe moisture before transport reduces breakage and spoilage. Use clean, dry gunny bags or bulk carriers.

harvest_indicators: Grain moisture at 20-25% for mechanical harvest
Panicles bend over with mature grains
Grain hardens and does not dent with fingernail
harvest_intelligence.harvest_timing: 110-130 days after sowing (depending on variety); harvest during dry weather to avoid grain damage
harvest_precautions: Do not delay harvest beyond physiological maturity to avoid shattering
Avoid harvesting during rain or high humidity
harvest_intelligence.expected_yield: 4-6 tons/ha (paddy) for improved varieties; up to 8 tons/ha for hybrid high-management systems

post_harvest_intelligence.drying: Dry paddy to 12-14% moisture content immediately after harvest; sun dry on clean mats or use mechanical dryers; avoid over-heating that causes cracks.
post_harvest_intelligence.cleaning: Winnow and clean to remove chaff, stones, weed seeds, and immature grains before storage or milling.
post_harvest_intelligence.grading: Grade paddy by size, colour, and moisture; separate damaged, broken, and immature grains to improve milling quality and market price.
post_harvest_intelligence.storage: Store in clean, dry, well-ventilated, pest-proof bins or gunny bags; use fumigation and moisture control; keep off the floor on pallets.
post_harvest_intelligence.transportation: Transport dried, cleaned grain in clean, dry bags or bulk carriers; protect from rain and moisture during transit.
post_harvest_intelligence.shelf_life: 6-12 months under proper storage conditions (moisture <14%, low humidity, pest controlled)
post_harvest_intelligence.quality_maintenance: Maintain low moisture, avoid insect infestation, and prevent fungal growth; store in cool, dry conditions with periodic inspection.

good_agricultural_practices: Use certified, disease-free seeds and proper seed treatment
Maintain optimum plant population and spacing
Practice timely weed control and field hygiene
climate_smart_practices: Use flood-tolerant varieties (Swarna Sub-1) in flood-prone areas
Adopt alternate wetting and drying to save water and reduce methane
Use drought-tolerant varieties in rainfed areas
Adjust sowing dates to match monsoon onset
sustainability_practices: Recycle rice straw into the field to maintain soil organic matter
Reduce chemical inputs with need-based LCC-based nitrogen
Conserve water through AWD and SRI
cost_optimisation: Use soil testing and LCC to reduce fertilizer costs
Adopt direct seeding where suitable to save labour
Procure inputs through cooperatives for better prices
yield_optimisation: Ensure water at critical stages (tillering, panicle initiation, flowering)
Harvest at correct maturity for maximum recovery

Germination.objectives: Achieve uniform, healthy seed germination and early root and shoot emergence.
Germination.growth_characteristics: Seed absorbs water, radical and plumule emerge, and the first leaves (coleoptile) break through the soil. Germination is fastest at 25-30°C.
Germination.water_principles: Maintain light, consistent moisture without waterlogging. Seed must be moist but not saturated to allow oxygen for germination.
Germination.sowing_guidance: Use certified, disease-free seeds. Treat seeds with a contact fungicide (e.g. carbendazim) before sowing. Presoak seeds for 12-24 hours and incubate for 24-48 hours to encourage uniform sprouting before sowing.
Germination.fertilizer_principles: Nutrient demand is minimal at germination. A light basal application supports early root establishment but avoid excess which can cause seedling burn.
Germination.nutrient_principles: Minimal nitrogen; seeds carry their own reserve. Phosphorus supports early root initiation.
Germination.timing_guidance: No fertilizer application needed at germination; ensure beds are prepared with basal compost if nursery raising.

fertilizer_logic.risk_if_skipped: Slower root establishment and weak early seedlings

Germination.fertilizer_weather_precautions: Avoid fertilizer application during heavy rain or waterlogged conditions that can wash nutrients away or cause seed rot.
Germination.fertilizer_focus: Minimal input; focus on moisture and temperature for successful germination
Germination.fertilizer_notes: Excess nitrogen at germination can cause 'damping-off' and seed rotting. Keep beds moist but well-drained.
Germination.soil_type_adjustment: Use well-drained, fine-tilth nursery beds. For sandy soils, maintain frequent light irrigation; for clay, avoid over-saturation.
Germination.deficiency_symptoms: Poor and uneven germination, seed rot, weak coleoptile, pale seedlings
Germination.fertilizer_avoidance: Avoid direct fertilizer contact with germinating seeds (seed burn)
Germination.organic_fertilizer_options: Well-decomposed compost or FYM in the nursery bed at 5-10 tons/ha improves soil structure and moisture retention.
Germination.cost_efficiency_guidance: Use seed priming and proper seed rate to ensure uniform stand and reduce seed wastage.

water_management.irrigation_frequency: Light moisture maintenance; irrigate as needed to keep soil damp
water_management.critical_condition: Avoid waterlogging and standing water during germination to prevent seed rot
water_management.water_stress_symptoms: Poor germination, drying and shrivelling of seeds, uneven emergence
water_management.recovery_guidance: Restore light moisture immediately; if germination is poor, re-sow with fresh treated seed

Seedling.objectives: Develop a vigorous, healthy seedling with strong roots for successful transplanting.
Seedling.growth_characteristics: Seedling develops 2-4 leaves, tillers begin, and a strong root system forms. Rapid growth responds to nitrogen and moisture.
Seedling.water_principles: Maintain light moisture without waterlogging. Frequent light irrigation every 2-3 days keeps nursery beds moist.
Seedling.sowing_guidance: Raise seedlings in well-prepared nursery beds; maintain 20-25 day old seedlings for transplanting at 2-3 seedlings per hill.
Seedling.fertilizer_principles: Apply nitrogen-rich basal fertilizer to support seedling vigor and early root development.
Seedling.nutrient_principles: Focus on Nitrogen for vigorous seedling growth and root development; light Phosphorus for root initiation.
Seedling.timing_guidance: Apply basal nitrogen before sowing or within 5-7 days after germination.

fertilizer_logic.risk_if_skipped: Weak seedling growth and poor establishment

Seedling.fertilizer_weather_precautions: Avoid fertilizer application during heavy rain or waterlogged conditions. Apply on moist soil for better nutrient uptake.
Seedling.fertilizer_focus: Nitrogen-based nutrition for seedling vigor and root establishment
Seedling.fertilizer_timing: Apply basal dose before sowing or within 5-7 days after germination
Seedling.fertilizer_notes: Seedlings respond well to light but frequent nitrogen. Avoid excess that causes lush growth prone to disease.
Seedling.soil_type_adjustment: For sandy soils, split nitrogen into small frequent doses; for clay, a single basal application at sowing is sufficient.
Seedling.deficiency_symptoms: Pale yellow leaves, stunted seedling growth, poor root development, purple tint on leaf margins
Seedling.fertilizer_avoidance: Avoid excess nitrogen that leads to soft, succulent growth vulnerable to damping-off
Seedling.organic_fertilizer_options: Well-decomposed FYM at 5-10 tons/ha or vermicompost improves seedling vigor.
Seedling.cost_efficiency_guidance: Use neem-coated urea to improve nitrogen use efficiency by 10-15% and reduce application frequency.

water_management.soil_moisture: Keep soil moist but not saturated
water_management.water_stress_symptoms: Wilting, leaf rolling, yellowing of seedlings
water_management.recovery_guidance: Restore moisture gradually; avoid overwatering; transplant only healthy, vigorous seedlings

Tillering.objectives: Maximize productive tiller production and canopy development for high yield potential.
Tillering.growth_characteristics: Plant develops productive tillers, increases leaf area, and builds a strong canopy. Nitrogen and water are critical for maximum tillering.
Tillering.water_principles: Maintain shallow standing water (2-5 cm) to promote tillering. Avoid prolonged dry periods.
Tillering.sowing_guidance: Transplant healthy 20-25 day old seedlings at proper spacing (20x15 cm). Maintain 2-3 seedlings per hill for optimum tillering.
Tillering.fertilizer_principles: Apply nitrogen and phosphorus for tillering and canopy development. Split nitrogen application for better efficiency.
Tillering.nutrient_principles: Focus on Nitrogen for maximum tiller production and Phosphorus for strong root and shoot development. Zinc is critical in submerged conditions.
Tillering.timing_guidance: Apply first top dressing of nitrogen at active tillering stage (20-25 days after transplanting). Second dose at 40-45 DAT if needed.

fertilizer_logic.risk_if_skipped: Reduced tillering, weak canopy, and poor yield potential

Tillering.fertilizer_weather_precautions: Apply fertilizer when soil is moist and no heavy rain is expected. Avoid application during continuous overcast or waterlogged conditions.
Tillering.fertilizer_focus: Nitrogen and phosphorus support for maximum tiller production and canopy development
Tillering.fertilizer_timing: Apply first top dressing at 20-25 DAT, second at 40-45 DAT if required
Tillering.fertilizer_notes: Zinc deficiency is common in submerged rice. Apply zinc sulfate at 25 kg/ha or 0.5% foliar spray if deficiency observed.
Tillering.soil_type_adjustment: For light-textured sandy soils, split nitrogen into 3-4 doses; for heavy clay soils, 2-3 splits are adequate.
Tillering.deficiency_symptoms: Yellowing of lower leaves (N), reduced tillering, stunted height, purple tinge on older leaves (P), leaf bronzing (Zn)
Tillering.fertilizer_avoidance: Avoid applying all nitrogen as basal. Excessive vegetative growth from over-fertilization increases lodging and disease risk.
Tillering.organic_fertilizer_options: Green manuring with dhaincha or sunn hemp incorporated before transplanting. Apply well-decomposed compost at 10-15 tons/ha.
Tillering.cost_efficiency_guidance: Use leaf color chart (LCC) for need-based nitrogen application to reduce costs by 20-25% while maintaining yield.

water_management.soil_moisture: Keep soil saturated with 2-5 cm standing water
water_management.water_stress_symptoms: Reduced tillering, leaf rolling, premature drying of leaves
water_management.recovery_guidance: Restore standing water promptly; if stress prolonged, apply light nitrogen to recover tiller production

Panicle_Initiation.objectives: Trigger panicle development and set the foundation for grain number and yield.
Panicle_Initiation.growth_characteristics: Panicle primordia begin to form at the base of the plant and move upward. The crop transitions from vegetative to reproductive growth; nutrient and water needs shift.
Panicle_Initiation.water_principles: Maintain continuous moisture with 2-5 cm standing water. Avoid any water stress as it severely limits panicle production.
Panicle_Initiation.sowing_guidance: Ensure a uniform, healthy crop stand; maintain plant population from earlier stages. Minimize stress during this transition.
Panicle_Initiation.fertilizer_principles: Apply potassium for panicle development and strong stems. Limit nitrogen to avoid excessive vegetative growth.
Panicle_Initiation.nutrient_principles: Potassium is critical for panicle development and stem strength. Limited nitrogen for panicle formation. Zinc and Boron support panicle and grain set.
Panicle_Initiation.timing_guidance: Apply potassium at panicle initiation (45-50 DAT). Apply nitrogen only if the crop is nitrogen-deficient.

fertilizer_logic.risk_if_skipped: Reduced panicle number, poor grain set, and yield loss

Panicle_Initiation.fertilizer_weather_precautions: Do not apply fertilizer if heavy rain or storm is forecast. Avoid foliar application during high temperature (>35°C) or windy conditions.
Panicle_Initiation.fertilizer_focus: Potassium for panicle development, stem strength, and stress resilience
Panicle_Initiation.fertilizer_timing: Apply potassium at panicle initiation (45-50 DAT). Add nitrogen only if deficiency is visible.
Panicle_Initiation.fertilizer_notes: This is a critical transition stage. Potassium strengthens stems and supports panicle assertion. Zinc and boron support grain set.
Panicle_Initiation.soil_type_adjustment: On sandy/light soils, split potassium into 2 doses; on clay soils, a single dose at panicle initiation is adequate.
Panicle_Initiation.deficiency_symptoms: Yellowing and drying of older leaf tips (K), weak stems, poor panicle emergence, increased chaffy grains
Panicle_Initiation.fertilizer_avoidance: Avoid excess nitrogen during panicle initiation as it increases blast severity and lodging risk.
Panicle_Initiation.organic_fertilizer_options: Apply potassium-rich organic sources like wood ash (10-15 kg/ha) or banana pseudostem compost.
Panicle_Initiation.cost_efficiency_guidance: Apply potassium based on soil test results to avoid over-application. Muriate of potash (MOP) is cost-effective.

Flowering.objectives: Ensure successful pollination and grain set for maximum filled grains.
Flowering.growth_characteristics: Panicles emerge and flowering (anthesis) occurs. Pollination is highly sensitive to temperature, water, and humidity. Spikelet sterility occurs under stress.
Flowering.water_principles: Maintain continuous moisture with 2-5 cm standing water. Never allow the field to dry during flowering to prevent spikelet sterility.
Flowering.sowing_guidance: Ensure a uniform crop stand entering flowering with adequate plant population. Maintain stable field conditions without stress.
Flowering.fertilizer_principles: Apply potassium and limited nitrogen for grain formation and pollination support. Avoid excess nitrogen during this stage.
Flowering.nutrient_principles: Focus on Potassium for grain filling and stress tolerance. Limited Nitrogen for panicle development. Boron and Zinc for pollen viability.
Flowering.timing_guidance: Apply potassium at panicle initiation stage (45-50 DAT) and a maintenance dose during early flowering if needed.

fertilizer_logic.application_method: Split application with adequate soil moisture
fertilizer_logic.risk_if_skipped: Poor pollination, reduced grain setting, and significant yield loss

Flowering.fertilizer_weather_precautions: Do not apply fertilizer if heavy rain or storm is forecast. Avoid foliar application during high temperature (>35°C) or windy conditions.
Flowering.fertilizer_focus: Potassium nutrition for grain development, stress resilience, and improved grain quality
Flowering.fertilizer_timing: Apply potassium at panicle initiation (45-50 DAT). Additional maintenance dose at early flowering if potassium deficiency is observed.
Flowering.fertilizer_notes: Potassium deficiency during flowering severely impacts grain filling and quality. Foliar potassium (2% KNO3) can be applied if deficiency symptoms appear.
Flowering.soil_type_adjustment: On sandy/light soils, split potassium into 2 doses; on clay soils, a single dose at panicle initiation is sufficient.
Flowering.deficiency_symptoms: Yellowing and drying of older leaf tips and margins (K), weak stems, poor panicle emergence, increased chaffy grains, lodging susceptibility
Flowering.fertilizer_avoidance: Avoid excess nitrogen during flowering as it increases blast disease severity and lodging risk. Avoid foliar sprays during peak heat hours.
Flowering.organic_fertilizer_options: Apply potassium-rich organic sources like wood ash (10-15 kg/ha) or banana pseudostem compost. Foliar spray of vermiwash or seaweed extract for micronutrients.
Flowering.cost_efficiency_guidance: Apply potassium based on soil test results to avoid over-application. Muriate of potash (MOP) is cost-effective and readily available.

Grain Filling.objectives: Fill grains to maximum weight and quality for high yield and milling recovery.
Grain Filling.growth_characteristics: Grains fill and gain weight as starch accumulates. Grain moisture declines. The crop is sensitive to water and nutrient stress, and lodging risk is present.
Grain Filling.water_principles: Controlled irrigation every 4-5 days. Maintain moist soil but avoid prolonged standing water to prevent lodging.
Grain Filling.sowing_guidance: Maintain optimal plant population from earlier stages for uniform grain development. Protect against lodging during this critical stage.
Grain Filling.fertilizer_principles: Focus on potassium support for grain weight development. Minimize nitrogen to avoid lush growth that delays maturity.
Grain Filling.nutrient_principles: Potassium is critical for grain filling and weight development. Minimal nitrogen needed. Micronutrients like zinc and boron aid grain quality.
Grain Filling.timing_guidance: Apply potassium at early grain filling stage if needed. Foliar micronutrients (Zn, B) can boost grain quality and weight.

fertilizer_logic.application_method: Foliar support if deficiency observed. Soil application during early grain filling.
fertilizer_logic.risk_if_skipped: Poor grain weight, reduced grain quality, and increased chaffy grains

Grain Filling.fertilizer_weather_precautions: Avoid fertilizer application if heavy rainfall or strong winds are forecast due to increased lodging risk.
Grain Filling.fertilizer_focus: Potassium and micronutrient support for optimal grain filling, weight development, and milling quality
Grain Filling.fertilizer_timing: Apply potassium at early grain filling (55-65 DAT). Foliar spray of 2% DAP or KNO3 if nutrient deficiency is visible.
Grain Filling.fertilizer_notes: Grain filling is highly sensitive to both nutrient and water stress. Nitrogen at this stage delays maturity by 5-7 days. Monitor potassium levels closely.
Grain Filling.soil_type_adjustment: Light/sandy soils may need split potassium application. Heavy clay soils typically retain adequate potassium from earlier applications.
Grain Filling.deficiency_symptoms: Chlorosis and premature drying of older leaves (K), weak stems, poor grain filling, lightweight and chaffy grains, increased lodging
Grain Filling.fertilizer_avoidance: Avoid late nitrogen application that delays maturity by 5-7 days and increases pest and disease attraction to tender new growth.
Grain Filling.organic_fertilizer_options: Foliar spray of compost tea or fermented plant extracts. Apply potassium-rich organic manure if soil test indicates deficiency.
Grain Filling.cost_efficiency_guidance: Tissue testing at early grain filling can identify specific nutrient deficiencies and avoid unnecessary fertilizer costs.

water_management.critical_condition: Avoid drought stress during grain development. Drain excess water to prevent lodging.
water_management.soil_moisture: Alternate wetting and drying. Keep soil moist but not continuously saturated.
water_management.ideal_soil_moisture: 70-80% field capacity with alternate wetting and drying
water_management.water_stress_symptoms: Incomplete grain filling, lightweight grains, premature drying of leaves
water_management.recovery_guidance: Restore moisture if stress occurs; avoid waterlogging; do not add late nitrogen

Grain Filling.nutrient_focus: Potassium; Zinc and Boron for grain quality

Harvest.objectives: Harvest at optimal maturity to maximize grain yield, quality, and milling recovery.
Harvest.growth_characteristics: Grain reaches physiological maturity and moisture declines. Leaves and stems senesce. The crop is ready for harvest when grains harden and turn golden.
Harvest.water_principles: Stop irrigation 10-15 days before harvest. Allow field to dry completely for easy harvesting and threshing operations.
Harvest.sowing_guidance: Plan harvest timing based on grain moisture content: 20-25% for mechanical harvest, 18-20% for manual harvest. Avoid delaying beyond optimal window.
Harvest.fertilizer_principles: No major fertilizer application required during harvest. Focus on harvest preparation and post-harvest soil management.
Harvest.nutrient_principles: Nutrient demand is minimal. Allow natural senescence for grain ripening. Focus on post-harvest nutrient replenishment for next cycle.
Harvest.timing_guidance: No routine fertilizer application during harvest. Stop all fertilization 2-3 weeks before harvest to allow natural ripening.

fertilizer_logic.risk_if_skipped: Minimal impact on current crop. Focus on post-harvest soil replenishment.

Harvest.fertilizer_weather_precautions: No fertilizer needed during this stage. Ensure dry weather window for harvest operations. Protect harvested grain from rain.
Harvest.fertilizer_focus: No fertilizer focus needed. Prioritize timely harvest and proper grain drying and storage.
Harvest.fertilizer_timing: No fertilizer application required during harvest stage. Resume fertilization for next crop cycle after harvest.
Harvest.fertilizer_notes: Stop all irrigation and fertilization 2-3 weeks before harvest to allow uniform ripening. Harvest at 20-25% grain moisture for optimal quality.
Harvest.soil_type_adjustment: All soil types: Focus on field drying rather than fertilizer management. After harvest, incorporate crop residue based on soil type.
Harvest.deficiency_symptoms: Premature leaf senescence and lodging in case of severe potassium exhaustion during grain filling. Otherwise, natural yellowing expected.
Harvest.fertilizer_avoidance: Avoid all fertilizer application during this stage to prevent delayed maturity and uneven ripening.
Harvest.organic_fertilizer_options: Apply compost, farmyard manure, or green manure after harvest to replenish soil organic matter and nutrients for the next crop cycle.
Harvest.cost_efficiency_guidance: Focus investment on efficient harvest timing and proper post-harvest handling to minimize grain losses rather than additional input costs.

water_management.critical_condition: Ensure field drying completely before harvesting to allow machinery access and prevent grain deterioration
water_management.soil_moisture: Allow field to dry naturally. Soil should be firm enough for harvest operations.
water_management.water_stress_symptoms: None expected; natural senescence and drying are normal
water_management.recovery_guidance: Not applicable for harvest; ensure grain is dried and handled promptly after harvest

diseases.name: Blast Disease
diseases.causes: Fungal pathogen (Magnaporthe oryzae) favoured by high humidity, excess nitrogen, and dense planting.
diseases.disease_progression: Leaf lesions appear first, spreading to sheaths and panicle neck; severe infection causes panicle blast and grain loss.
diseases.treatment: Apply tricyclazole or carbendazim at early symptom appearance; remove infected debris; follow label recommendations.
diseases.weather_relationships: High humidity, rainfall, and cool nights (20-30°C) favour blast development.

diseases.name: Sheath Blight
diseases.causes: Fungal pathogen (Rhizoctonia solani) favoured by high humidity, dense canopy, and excess nitrogen.
diseases.disease_progression: Lesions on leaf sheaths spread upward to flag leaf and panicle; severe infection reduces grain filling and causes lodging.
diseases.treatment: Apply hexaconazole or validamycin at early symptoms; reduce nitrogen and improve drainage.
diseases.weather_relationships: High humidity, dense canopy, and warm temperatures (25-32°C) favour sheath blight.

diseases.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight
visible_symptoms: Yellow to white lesions with wavy margins
Milky bacterial ooze on cut leaves
diseases.causes: Bacterial pathogen (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae) spread by wind, rain, and infected seed.
diseases.disease_progression: Lesions begin at leaf tips and margins, spreading downward; severe infection causes leaf wilting and yield loss.
prevention_logic: Avoid field flooding that spreads bacteria
diseases.treatment: Apply streptocycline + copper oxychloride at early symptoms; use resistant varieties; avoid excessive nitrogen.
diseases.weather_relationships: High humidity, rainfall, and wind-driven spread favour bacterial leaf blight.

diseases.name: Brown Spot
diseases.causes: Fungal pathogen (Bipolaris oryzae) favoured by nutrient deficiency, water stress, and humid conditions.
diseases.disease_progression: Brown spots appear on leaves and grains; severe infection reduces photosynthesis and grain quality.
diseases.treatment: Apply mancozeb or propiconazole; improve nutrition and drainage.
diseases.weather_relationships: High humidity, water stress, and nutrient deficiency favour brown spot.

pests.name: Brown Plant Hopper (BPH)
visible_symptoms: Hopper burn (yellowing and drying of plants)
pests.damage: BPH sucks sap from plant bases, causing hopper burn and rapid plant death in patches.
pests.treatment: Apply pymetrozine or buprofezin at threshold levels; drain field to reduce humidity; protect natural enemies.
pests.weather_relationships: Warm, humid conditions and continuous cropping favour BPH outbreaks.

pests.name: Stem Borer
pests.damage: Stem borer larvae tunnel into stems, causing dead hearts and whiteheads that reduce yield.
pests.treatment: Apply chlorantraniliprole or cartap hydrochloride at threshold levels; remove and destroy egg masses.
pests.weather_relationships: Dry spells and warm conditions favour stem borer activity.

pests.name: Leaf Folder
visible_symptoms: Leaf blades folded and tied with silk
pests.damage: Leaf folder larvae fold and feed on leaves, reducing photosynthetic area and yield.
pests.treatment: Apply chlorantraniliprole or flubendiamide at threshold levels; avoid broad-spectrum sprays.
pests.weather_relationships: High humidity and lush vegetative growth favour leaf folder activity.

pests.name: Earhead Bug (Grain Sucking Bug)
pests.damage: Earhead bugs suck sap from developing grains, causing chaffy, empty grains and reduced quality.
pests.treatment: Apply recommended insecticide at heading and grain filling; time applications to protect natural enemies.
pests.weather_relationships: Warm, humid conditions favour earhead bug multiplication.

pests.name: Rice Hispa
visible_symptoms: White streaky feeding lines on leaves
pests.damage: Hispa larvae and adults feed on leaf tissue, reducing photosynthetic area and plant vigor.
pests.treatment: Apply recommended insecticide (e.g. chlorantraniliprole) at early infestation; remove infected leaves.
pests.weather_relationships: High humidity and wet conditions favour hispa activity.
